key_invariants: If the target is present, it remains within the inclusive interval [left, right].
Every non-matching comparison moves one bound past midpoint, so the interval strictly shrinks.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: int search(vector<int> a,int t){int l=0,r=a.size()-1;while(l<=r){int m=l+(r-l)/2;if(a[m]==t)return m;if(a[m]<t)l=m+1;else r=m-1;}return -1;} };
class Solution { public int search(int[] a,int t){int l=0,r=a.length-1;while(l<=r){int m=l+(r-l)/2;if(a[m]==t)return m;if(a[m]<t)l=m+1;else r=m-1;}return -1;} }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: The target remains in the interval if present.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Explain why each comparison halves the range.

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: Retain inclusive endpoints long enough to find the first or last element.
Terminate with -1 after the inclusive interval becomes empty.

sample_phrasings: What ensures this interval keeps shrinking?

level_considerations.guidance: Focus on interval invariants and boundary reasoning.
